My research develops and applies spatial and spatiotemporal statistical methods, with a focus on how we build and fairly evaluate predictive models for environmental data. Below are the projects I am currently working on.

::: research-card
### Predicting in-lake turbidity from satellite data

```{=html}
<!-- Add a map or satellite figure here when ready:
![](images/research/turbidity.png){.research-image fig-alt="Satellite-based turbidity predictions across a lake"}
-->
```

This project uses satellite imagery to predict turbidity within a lake. One part compares spatial models for making these predictions. Another simulates boat sampling paths to compare cross-validation strategies for judging predictive accuracy.

**Collaborators:** M. S. Macleod, S. M. Powers, A. S. Hering\
**Outputs:** Presented at the UCOWR/NIWR Annual Water Resources Conference (2026); manuscript in preparation. See [Publications & Conferences](publications-conferences.qmd).
:::

::: research-card
### Mapping public water data across Texas

<!-- ![](images/research/water-data.png){.research-image fig-alt="Network of Texas water data organizations"} -->

As part of the Baylor Water Security Collaborative, I am inventorying and characterizing public water data resources across Texas, documenting coverage, access methods, and citation practices to identify statewide data gaps. We are framing this inventory as a network, with the organizations that collect, aggregate, and use water data as nodes and the data flows between them as connections.

**Collaborators:** A. S. Hering and the Baylor Water Security Collaborative
:::
